subject: Post-demo: tool/function stack selection and error-handling matrix for EdgePay POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@edgepay.com>, Miguel Fernandez <miguel@edgepay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: tool/function stack selection and error-handling matrix for EdgePay POC

Hey Tara / Miguel —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap (short):
- Goal: 6-week POC to validate (a) SDK integration + auth, (b) structured tool/function calling for payments support actions, (c) embeddings + reranker for matching KB articles to intents.
- Scope we sketched: SDK quickstart (server + client), one tool for 'charge-capture' (internal API call), one for 'refund-lookup' (customer-facing), reranker on top of embeddings for top-3 KB answers.

Open technical asks we promised to clarify:
1) Auth model: will EdgePay prefer a token-per-service (short-lived) or centralized service-account for server-side calls?
2) Routing policy: strict latency vs. cost preference per route (e.g., charge-capture must be low-latency; KB rerank can be batched).
3) Tool semantics: do tools need idempotency keys, step-level compensation, or purely synchronous fire-and-return?

Proposed options (we'll own a one-page decision matrix):
A) Minimal path (fastest): Redwood SDK (server) + hosted model for generation + single dedicated function endpoint on your side for charge-capture. Tool calls synchronous, rely on idempotency token at application layer.
B) Production guardrails (recommended): SDK + private deployment stub for sensitive flows, function calling with declared tool schema (inputs/outputs), enforced structured JSON responses, automatic retries with exponential backoff + safe dedupe using request-id header. Also set up a small reranker service using embeddings stored in your managed repo (S3) with nightly refresh.
C) High-availability: add parallel tool fanout for charge-capture (primary -> fallback region/model) with winner-takes-all commit only after optimistic pre-check; introduces complexity but improves SLA.

Next concrete steps I suggest:
- We send a draft "tool-definitions" CSV and an error-handling matrix for you to review (attached).
- Technical drop-in: Priyom + Vanessa propose Wed 10/07 9:00-10:00 PT for SDK/auth walkthrough and to lock routing choices.
- Security ask: Tara, please share your preferred evidence artifact list (SOC2 scope, allowed egress, KMS requirements) — we'll attach a stub security bundle in reply.

Attachments: edgepay-poc-sow.pdf (scope), tool-definitions-v1.csv (tool schemas + metadata).

Would love confirmation on the Wed slot and the preferred auth model.

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: Re: Post-demo: tool/function stack selection and error-handling matrix for EdgePay POC

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side:

Auth: we prefer service-account tokens for server-to-server right now (centralized KMS), but for client-side (mobile) flows we'll need short-lived delegated tokens. So we need both patterns documented.

Routing: agreed that charge-capture is latency-sensitive; reranker can be batched. Also call out data residency — US-only for anything PII.

Tool semantics: our internal charge-capture API is idempotent by transaction_id, but the gateway we integrate with sometimes returns transient 5xxs. We want retries with jitter up to 3 attempts, and a dead-letter route for manual review if still failing.

On the parallel/fanout option — it's attractive but let's get the basic flow working first. If the POC shows >250 rps we can evaluate.

Wed 10/07 9:00 PT works for us for the technical walkthrough. Tara will follow up with the security artifact checklist.

-Miguel

Quick internal-tech note (putting up our proposed option set so we can present Wed):

1) SDK/Auth patterns to propose on the call:
- Server (recommended): Redwood SDK server-side auth using mTLS + short-lived tokens issued by Redwood control plane. For EdgePay we can map to your KMS via HSM-KMS integration so private keys never leave your envelope.
- Client: OAuth/OIDC flow issuing scoped ephemeral tokens via your auth broker (we'll show code snippets).

2) Tool definitions (structured):
- We recommend declaring tool schemas in the CSV (attached) with: tool_id, input_schema (JSON Schema URI), output_schema, idempotency_key_field, timeout_ms, retry_policy. Example: charge_capture -> input includes transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, customer_id; output must be exactly {"status":"succeeded|failed|retry","provider_ref":"...","errors":[]}.

3) Parallel tool fanout & dedupe rules:
- If you enable primary/fallback fanout, we will emit a correlation_id and require only one commit path to call your internal confirm endpoint. Support two modes: optimistic (first successful wins) and consensus (majority). We should avoid split-brain by enforcing a commit token exchange.

4) Error handling matrix (proposal highlights):
- 4xx from tool -> map to user error immediately, no retry.
- 5xx / transient -> retry up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter, then escalate to DLQ and create a support ticket via webhooks.
- Unexpected schema mismatch -> safe fail: return structured error to client and capture original payload to an audit bucket for replay.

5) Embeddings + reranker:
- We'll compute short (1536-d) embeddings for KB content, store vector store in your S3/GCS, and run a lightweight ANN (FAISS/Annoy) in the POC. Reranker will be a small generation model run as second-stage with top-10 candidates. Latency targets: 150ms tail for top-3 rerank when warmed.

6) Observability hooks: attach request-id, tool-id, model-variant, region in traces. We'll provide a sample tracing header and an integration doc for your logging team.

I'll prepare a one-pager decision matrix and a sample tool schema file to share before Wed. Anything else you want covered?

- Priyom

Thanks Ben / Priyom —

Appreciate the clear options. A couple quick items from Security/Platform:
- We'll upload the SOC2 excerpt + KMS requirements to the Drive link you shared. Expect a short checklist by EOD today.
- We need data residency enforced (US-only) and explicit encryption-at-rest keys (vendor-managed keys are fine if they map to our KMS via key wrapping).
- For the DLQ / support ticket flow: please include an idempotent webhook so our on-call can safely replay events.

Confirmed Wed 10/07 9:00-9:45 PT for the technical walkthrough — Miguel + I will join.

Action items we expect from Redwood before the call:
1) Draft tool-definitions-v1.csv (received) + short mapping doc that ties each tool to the expected retry/timeout semantics (Priyom's matrix).
2) One-page decision matrix covering: a) auth patterns b) routing policy templates (latency-first / cost-first) c) fallback modes for charge-capture.
3) Security stub (security-evidence-stub.zip) with SOC2 excerpt and encryption notes.

We will review and provide feedback on the CSV. Looking forward to the walkthrough.

-Tara
